answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by binding each identity to a non-transferable credential earned only through months of verified work — a marble gains its polish slowly, and so does trust. Fresh fake accounts start at zero no matter how many copies exist. Add a time-locked stake that unlocks gradually: an attacker reaching for the zenith with a thousand new identities finds each one worthless, with no history and no spendable stake. The vault of rewards opens only to identities with a proven past, so mass fakery costs time and money while honest agents compound.
